attributes.name: The World of: Radiohead’s ‘OK Computer’
attributes.description: “Fitter, happier, more productive” … Was any work of pop-music art more prescient in the late ’90s, or in any epoch, than Radiohead’s third studio LP? Released in 1997, its ironic dichotomy — a fearful meditation on tech-dependent postmodern life, awash in ingenious futuristic sounds and recording strategies — seems to embody our contemporary world of forced wellness and smartphone addiction. To celebrate the 25th anniversary of this essential album, we researched this special ‘World of’ playlist featuring the original tracks, their specific sonic and musical inspirations, the band’s more general influences during the period, other songs from this important moment in British alternative rock and more.

attributes.name: Radiohead Essentials
attributes.description: Modern rock history wouldn’t have been the same without Radiohead – a British ‘90s sensation that became one of the most influential alternative bands of all time. The five members – Thom Yorke (vocals, guitar), Ed O'Brien (guitar, vocals), Jonny Greenwood (guitar), Colin Greenwood (bass), and Phil Selway (drums) – formed Radiohead in 1988 while attending boarding school in Oxford. Initially called ‘On a Friday’ (referring to the day of the week they would meet up to rehearse) the band began a musical career that sharply took off with the celebrated 1993 debut Pablo Honey (and hit single “Creep”) and the classic follow-up The Bends (1995). But it was with the progressive, timeless, electronic-tinged masterpiece OK Computer (1997) that Radiohead became an international phenomenon. Since then, the band has brilliantly managed to continually evolve and reinvent themselves, always trying out new sounds and musical directions, such as with the two-part electronic suite Kid A (2000) and Amnesiac (2001). As one of the most celebrated acts of their time, Radiohead have never really made a mediocre album. (Photo: Rovi)

attributes.name: NME: Greatest Songs of All Time
attributes.description: NME has compiled a list of the best songs of all time - and not just any list. According to the British weekly and website, this is "the definitive countdown of the best tracks ever recorded." (Photo: logo)

attributes.name: Remember...the 1990s
attributes.description: The 1990s - what a memorable decade! R.E.M. and U2 ascended as world stars, while grunge changed many people's perception of what could top the charts. Pop-punk (Green Day, The Offspring) and Britpop (Oasis, Blur) were born, just as hip-hop was gaining traction on the charts (Jay-Z, Eminem). Many promising hitmakers would go on to have long, healthy careers, while others would never see the 2000s. But they all belong in our collective memory of the 1990's. (Cover: The Notorious B.I.G. - Ready to Die, Bad Boy/WMG)
